:::{#exm-surprisal-coins}
#### Counting bits with fair coins

One toss of a fair coin has $2$ equally likely outcomes,
and one binary digit is enough to record which one happened.
Two tosses have $4$ outcomes, and two binary digits record them.
In general, $n$ equally likely outcomes take $\log_2 n$ binary digits.

Each of those $n$ outcomes has probability $p = 1/n$, so

$$
\begin{aligned}
\log_2 n
&= \log_2 \frac{1}{p} \\
&= -\log_2 p,
\end{aligned}
$$

which is the [surprisal](#def-surprisal) of the outcome, in bits.

Ten tosses that all land heads have probability $2^{-10}$, so

$$
\begin{aligned}
s(\text{ten heads})
&= -\log_2 2^{-10} \\
&= 10 \text{ bits}.
\end{aligned}
$$

:::
